title: reports lions rework deals 2 stars free up 357m  flm 2026 09 12
text:
Sep 12 (Field Level Media) - The Detroit Lions restructured the contracts of wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown and left tackle Penei ​Sewell and created $35.68 million in cap space, ‌multiple outlets reported Saturday.
The Lions now rank second in the league in available cap space at about $38 million, ​which can also be carried over to 2027, ​according to Over The Cap and Spotrac.
Detroit ⁠now has the freedom to make an in-season ​move before the trade deadline or work on ​long-term extensions with tight end Sam LaPorta and safety Brian Branch.
Sewell, 25, signed a four-year, $112 million contract extension with $85 million ​guaranteed in April 2024. The three-time All-Pro ​has started all 83 of his games since the Lions ‌drafted ⁠him seventh overall in 2021.
St. Brown, 26, also signed an extension in April 2024, a four-year, $120 million deal with $77 million guaranteed. The two-time All-Pro has ​547 catches ​for 6,252 ⁠yards and 44 touchdowns in 83 games (75 starts) since Detroit drafted him in ​the fourth round in 2021.
According to ​the reports, ⁠the Lions converted $18.6 million of Sewell's salary in a signing bonus, added one void year to ⁠his ​contract and created $14.8 million in cap ​space. They converted $26 million of St. Brown's salary into a ​signing bonus to free up another $20.8 million.
--Field Level Media
